newsitem.title: CANADA: Three killed in western Canada plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Three killed in western Canada plane crash.

text.p: Three people were killed on Friday when their single-engine plane crashed near the border of Saskatchewan and Alberta in western Canada.

A rescue crew picked up an emergency signal just before the plane crashed on farmland near Marsden, Saskatchewan, about 150 miles (240 kms) northwest of Saskatoon, Cpl. Gerry Baragar of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police said.
Rescuers were sent by helicopter from a nearby military base and found the wreckage and bodies, Baragar said.
He said it was unlikely that weather conditions played a role in the incident. "It's cold, but it's cold and calm. I have no idea what could have caused it," he said.
The identities of the pilot and two passengers as well as the aircraft's destination were not immidiately known.
